The '''2019–20 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team''' represented [[Georgetown University]] in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hoyas, led by third-year head coach [[Patrick Ewing]], played their home games at the [[Capital One Arena]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], as members of the [[Big East Conference]]. They lost to [[2019–20 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] in the first round of the [[2020 Big East men's basketball tournament]], finished with a record of 15–17 overall and 5–13 in Big East play, and had no postseason play.

==Previous season==
The [[2018–19 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Hoyas]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] at 19–14, 9–9 in [[2018–19 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]], to finish in sixth place in the conference. As the No. 6 seed in the [[2019 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they lost in the first round to [[2018–19 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]]. Invited to the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]], they lost in the first round to [[2018–19 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team|Harvard]]. Georgetown finished the season with a winning record, a non-losing conference record, and an invitation to a postseason tournament, all for the first time since [[2014–15 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2014–15]].

==Season recap==

In addition to sophomore [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] Antwan Walker – dismissed from the team in October 2018, he subsequently had transferred to [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] – Georgetown had lost five players since the conclusion of [[2018–19 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the previous season]]: [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] Greg Malinowski, guard/forward Kaleb Johnson, forward [[Trey Mourning]], and [[Center (basketball)|center]] [[Jessie Govan]] all had graduated in 2019, and freshman forward Grayson Carter had transferred to [[UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|UT Arlington]] in search of greater playing time after a single season as a Hoya. However, a core of veteran players – sophomore James Akinjo at [[point guard]], senior Jagan Mosely, junior Jahvon Blair, and sophomore [[Mac McClung]] at guard, and junior Jamorko Pickett and sophomore Josh LeBlanc at forward — returned. Senior forward George Muresan, the son of former NBA player [[Gheorghe Muresan]], made the team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] for the fourth straight season. Sophomore guard Jaden Robinson also returned, making the team as a walk-on for the second straight year.

An addition for 2019–2020 was center [[Ömer Yurtseven]], a transfer from [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]] who joined the team as a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] junior after sitting out the previous season in accordance with NCAA transfer rules. Also arriving were guard Terrell Allen, a graduate transfer from [[UCF Knights men's basketball|Central Florida]] who had spent a season at [[Drexel Dragons men's basketball|Drexel]] before two years at UCF, and junior [[small forward]] Galen Alexander; recruited out of high school, Alexander had signed with [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], was dismissed from the team there without ever playing a game amid allegations that he had fired [[Paintball equipment#Paintballs|paintballs]] at other students, and subsequently spent two years at [[Jones County Junior College]].<ref name=banners20191029>[https://www.bannersontheparkway.com/2019/10/29/20938188/georgetown-team-preview-does-patrick-ewing-have-the-hoyas-on-the-right-track-big-east-xavier Brad D, "Georgetown team preview: Does Patrick Ewing have the Hoyas on the right track?," bannersontheparkway.com, October 29, 2019, 11:57 a.m. EDT Retrieved March 20, 2020 Retrieved March 20, 2020]</ref> Five freshmen — centers Timothy Ighoefe, Qudus Wahab, and Malcolm Wilson, forward [[Myron Gardner]], and recruited walk-on Chuma Azinge,<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2019/5/7/18534922/links-chuma-azinge-roster-recruiting-news-ewing-mourning-jalen-cook-wahab-broadus Whipple, "LINKS: Chuma Azinge, Roster & Recruiting News," casualhoya.com, May 7, 2019, 8:30 a.m. EDT Retrieved March 19, 2020]</ref> a guard — rounded out the team.

There were nine returning players from the previous season including four of that year's five starters,<ref name=akinjotabbed/> freshman standouts Akinjo, LeBlanc, and McClung among them,<ref name=swinton20191018>[https://www.si.com/college/2019/10/18/big-east-basketball-predictions-rankings Swinton, Elizabeth, "Big East Preview: Villanova, Seton Hall Lead Intriguing Group of Challengers," si.com, October 18, 2019 Retrieved March 14, 2020]</ref> as well as Yurtseven, replacing the departed Govan<ref name=swinton20191018/> and Alexander.

===2019 Bahamas Foreign Tour===

Under [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) rules, the Hoyas were allowed to make an overseas preseason trip to play exhibition games against foreign teams once every four years, and the 2019–2020 team followed up recent trips to [[China]] in [[2011–12 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|August 2011]] and [[Italy]] in [[2015–16 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|August 2015]] with a trip to the [[Bahamas]] — dubbed the "2019 Bahamas Foreign Tour"<ref name=guhoyas20190812>[http://guhoyas.com/news/2019/8/12/georgetown-mens-basketball-opens-foreign-tour-with-103-77-win.aspx Anonymous, "Georgetown Men’s Basketball Opens Foreign Tour with 103-77 Win," guhoyas.com, August 12, 2019, 10:14:00 p.m. EDT Retrieved August 17, 2019]</ref> — from August 10 to 17.<ref>[https://guhoyas.com/news/2019/5/15/mens-basketball-georgetown-heads-to-bahamas-for-2019-summer-tour.aspx Anonymous, "Georgetown Heads to Bahamas for 2019 Summer Tour," guhoyas.com, May 15, 2019, 11:00:00 a.m. EDT]</ref> The Hoyas held 10 team practices prior to the tour, the number permitted before an overseas tour by NCAA rules.<ref name=casualhoya20190809>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2019/8/9/20799102/links-georgetown-previews-business-trip-episode-2-schedule-roy-hibbert-jessie-govan-mulmore Anonymous, "Georgetown Previews ‘Business Trip’; Hibbert Coaching in NBA?," casualhoya.com, August 9, 2019, 4:30 p.m. EDT Retrieved August 17, 2019]</ref> Before departing, the team characterized the Bahamas visit as a "business trip;"<ref name=casualhoya20190809/> Patrick Ewing said that he wanted to use the trip to test different line-ups and gain insight into which of his players were sharing the ball and playing as a team, while James Akinjo and Mac McClung both expressed a desire to get to know their new teammates and learn how best to work together with them on the court, Josh LeBlanc said he wanted to focus on ball-sharing and team play, and Ömer Yurtseven planned to use the Bahamas games to get back into his competitive basketball routine after sitting out the 2018–2019 season.<ref name=casualhoya20190809/>

===Nonconference schedule===

In October, the Big East's coaches picked Georgetown to finish sixth in the 10-team conference in their annual preseason poll.<ref name=akinjotabbed>[http://guhoyas.com/news/2019/10/10/mens-basketball-akinjo-tabbed-preseason-second-team-at-big-east-media-day.aspx Anonymous, "Akinjo Tabbed Preseason Second Team at BIG EAST Media Day", October 10, 2019, 2:20 p.m. EDT Retrieved March 14, 2020]</ref> Akinjo — who the previous season had become the seventh Hoya to be selected as Big East Freshman of the Year<ref name=akinjotabbed/> — was selected to the Preseason All-Big East Second Team,<ref name=akinjotabbed/> and Yurtseven — who had averaged 13.5 points and 6.7 rebounds per game during his last season of play in [[2017-18 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|2017–2018]] with North Carolina State<ref name=akinjotabbed/> — won Preseason All-Big East Honorable Mention.<ref name=akinjotabbed/> In a preseason evaluation of the [[2019–20 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East for 2019–2020]], ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' picked the Hoyas to finish fifth in the Big East and identified the Georgetown squad as a solid mid-tier team in the conference with the potential to make a surprise run at the conference championship.<ref name=swinton20191018/>

The Hoyas opened the season on November 6 at [[Capital One Arena]] by shooting only 30 percent from the field against [[2019–20 Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball team|Mount St. Mary's]] in the first half, falling behind 37–25 at halftime. In the second half they shot 65.6 percent and finished with a 20–1 run, winning 81–68.<ref name=ap20191106>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168383 Anonymous, "Georgetown defeats Mount St. Mary's 81-68," Associated Press, November 6, 2019 Retrieved March 14, 2020]</ref> Ömer Yursteven had a [[double-double]] in his Georgetown debut with 20 points on 7–for–9 shooting and 12 rebounds, while James Akinjo also finished with 20 points and Mac McClung scored 16.<ref name=ap20191106/><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401168383 Mount St. Mary's vs. Georgetown – Box Score – November 6, 2019 – ESPN Retrieved March 14, 2020]</ref> Georgetown then began play in the [[2K Sports Classic|Empire Classic]], meeting [[2019–20 Central Arkansas Bears basketball team|Central Arkansas]] in an unbracketed game at Capital One Arena and defeating the Bears behind another Yurtseven double-double (17 points and 15 rebounds), 13 points by Jagan Moseley, and 10 by Jamorko Pickett.<ref name=ap20191109>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168384 Anonymous, "Yurtseven carries Georgetown past Cent. The following evening, Georgetown advanced to the Empire Classic championship game to face No. 1 [[2019–20 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]].<ref runs with scoring runs of their own to post leads of 22–12 and then 29–18, their largest of the game, with 6:11 left in the first half.<ref Georgetown suffered a setback eight days later when they finished November with an upset loss at home at the hands of [[2019–20 UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball team|UNC Greensboro]] in which James Akinjo scored 12 points, Yurtseven narrowly missed a double-double with 10 points and nine rebounds, and Jamorko Pickett finished with eight rebounds.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168387 Anonymous, "Langley lifts UNC-Greensboro over Georgetown 65-61," Associated Press, November 30, 2019 Retrieved March 14, 2020]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401168387 UNC Greensboro vs. Georgetown – Box Score – November 30, 2019 – ESPN Retrieved March 14, 2020]</ref> Georgetown's record dropped to 4–3. On December 2 Ewing announced that both James Akinjo and Josh LeBlanc would not play for Georgetown again and would transfer. On the same day, news broke that a Georgetown student and her roommate had filed [[restraining order]]s against LeBlanc, Galen Alexander, and [[Myron Gardner]] on November 5 and 12, alleging "sexual harassment and assault" by Gardner on September 15, a burglary of their apartment by LeBlanc, Alexander, and Gardner on September 16, and subsequent threats of bodily harm against both women by LeBlanc during the week following the alleged burglary, and that campus police and the [[Metropolitan Police Department of the District of Columbia]] were investigating the allegations; Akinjo was not implicated in any of the complaints.<ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigeast/2019/12/03/georgetown-basketball-leblanc-alexander-garnder-harassment-restraining-order/2594121001/ Bumbaca, Chris, "Georgetown players accused of harassment, burglary, assault," usatoday.com, December 3, 2019 1:04 p.m. EST Retrieved March 14, 2020.]</ref> Alexander and Gardner remained with the team, but Georgetown lost two of its top five scorers,<ref name=ap20191204>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168388 Anonymous, "McClung leads short-handed Georgetown over Oklahoma State," Associated Press, December 4, 2019 Retrieved March 15, 2020]</ref> one of them its starting point guard. "Last year, they were part of the heart and soul of our team," Ewing said two days later.<ref name=ap20191204/>

With a depleted roster, Georgetown made a road trip to play [[2019–20 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Oklahoma State]] and [[2019–20 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]]. In the Oklahoma State game — part of the first edition of the annual [[Big East–Big XII Alliance|Big East-Big 12 Battle]], which pitted Big East schools against those of the [[Big 12 Conference]] — Terrell Allen took over as starting point guard<ref name=ap20191204/> and the Hoyas won despite 29 points, six rebounds, and six assists by Cowboys senior guard Lindy Waters III.<ref name=ap20191204/> The Hoyas built an early lead, lost it early in the second half, but came from behind for the with a season-high 33 points by Mac McClung<ref name=ap20191204/><ref name=boxscore20191204>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401168388 Georgetown vs. Oklahoma State – Box Score – December 4, 2019 – ESPN Retrieved March 15, 2020]</ref> — Ewing called it "one of his best games as a Hoya"<ref name=ap20191204/> — 19 points and nine rebounds by Ömer Yurtseven,<ref name=ap20191204/><ref name=boxscore20191204/> a season-high 15 points and five assists by Allen,<ref name=ap20191204/><ref name=boxscore20191204/> and a 43–29 team rebounding performance, including 25–7 in the second half.<ref name=ap20191204/> Three nights later against undefeated SMU — the final game of a home-and-home series between the schools begun the previous season — Jahvon Blair came off the bench to tie his career high with 21 points,<ref name=ap20191207>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168389 Anonymous, "Blair scores 21 to lift Georgetown over SMU 91-74," Associated Press, December 7, 2019 Retrieved March 15, 2020]</ref><ref name=boxscore20191207>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401168389 Georgetown vs. SMU – Box Score – December 7, 2019 – ESPN Retrieved March 15, 2020]</ref> McClung contributed 19 points and seven assists,<ref name=ap20191207/> Yurtseven also scored 19,<ref name=ap20191207/> and Jamorko Pickett added 11<ref name=ap20191207/> as Georgetown improved its record to 6–3 with a second consecutive win. Galen Alexander and Myron Gardner played in both games, but on December 13 both of them announced their departure from the team and intention to transfer from Georgetown, Alexander blaming Georgetown for failing to support him against what he claimed were false charges against him in the alleged burglary case.<ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/12/13/alexander-gardner-leave-georgetown-team-plan-to-transfer/40822313/ Anonymous, "Galen Alexander, Myron Gardner leave Georgetown team, plan to transfer," Associated Press, December 13, 2019 11:53 p.m. EST Retrieved 15 March 2020]</ref> The loss of Alexander and Gardner left the team extremely shorthanded for the season, with only nine scholarship players remaining on the roster.<ref>[https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2019/12/13/georgetown-is-down-to-nine-scholarship-players-after-two-more-announce-transfer-plans/#7ed5faf5b105 Zagoria, Adam, "Georgetown Is Down To Nine Scholarship Players After Two More Announce Transfer Plans," forbes.com, December 13, 2019, 7:51 p.m. EST Retrieved March 18, 2020]</ref> Ewing told his remaining players that the team still had the talent to put together a successful season,<ref name=ap20191214/> but for the remainder of the season he was forced to play his remaining starters for long stretches with very little rest during games<ref name=ap20191214/> and give walk-ons greater playing team when turning to his depleted bench.<ref name=ap20191214/>

The annual game the previous year between Georgetown and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] — [[Georgetown–Syracuse men's basketball rivalry|longtime rivals]] in the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|original Big East Conference]] of 1979–2013 — had ended amid speculation that the schools would not play again in the near future because the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]'s decision to go to a 20-game conference schedule in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2019–2020]] would make it too difficult for the Orange to schedule Georgetown.<ref>[https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2018/12/is_the_future_of_syracuse_basketballs_rivalry_with_georgetown_in_jeopardy.html Waters, Mike, "Will Syracuse basketball's rivalry with Georgetown come to a close after Saturday?," syracuse.com, December 5, 2018 Retrieved March 19, 2019]</ref><ref>[https://www.nunesmagician.com/2018/12/12/18137955/syracuse-vs-georgetown-will-continue-for-as-long-as-acc-scheduling-allows-orange-baskebtall-hoyas Cassillo, John, "Syracuse vs. Georgetown will continue for as long as ACC scheduling allows," nunesmagician.com, December 12, 2018 1:45 p.m. EST Retrieved March 19, 2019]</ref> However, the teams continued the series ans, a week after defeating SMU and the day after Alexander and Gardner departed, Georgetown concluded the non-conference portion of their season with a four-game homestand at Capital One Arena that opened against [[2019–20 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]]. Georgetown finished non-conference play having overcome the loss of four players to win all six games they had played since the departure of Akinjo and LeBlanc, posting a record of 10–3 against non-conference opponents for the second season in a row, and defeating three opponents from the Power Five conferences.<ref name=ap20200205>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168400 Anonymous, "Powell scores 34, No. 12 Seton Hall beats Georgetown 78-71," February 5, 2020 Retrieved March 17, 2020]</ref> However, the non-conference portion of the season ended amid concerns that Georgetown's lack of depth after December's scandals and transfers would hurt the team in Big East play.<ref name=ap20191214/>

===Conference schedule===

Georgetown opened its Big East conference schedule on the road with a [[New Year's Eve]] game at [[2019–20 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]]. Still nursing his injured eye, Mac McClung missed the game.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2019/12/31/21044940/reports-mcclung-out-for-georgetowns-big-east-opener-at-providence-on-nye Bancroft, ===Big East tournament===
{{main|2020 Big East men's basketball tournament}}

Georgetown was seeded eighth in the [[2020 Big East men's basketball tournament|2020 Big East tournament]]. In the first round, played on March 11, the Hoyas faced St. John's, which had finished the regular season tied with the Hoyas but was seeded ninth based on tie-breaking criteria, which gave the nod to Georgetown for sweeping the regular-season series between the teams. It was the third time in four years that the teams had met in the first round of the tournament,<ref name=ap20200311>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401210943 Anonymous, "St. John's grabs momentum to down Georgetown," Associated Press, March 11, 2020 Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref> playing in the eight-vs.-nine game in each case.<ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/3/11/21174389/big-east-tournament-time-georgetown-vs-st-johns Bancroft, Bobby, "Big East tournament Time: Georgetown vs St. John’s," casualhoya.com, March 11, 2020, 8:00 am EDT Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref> Recovering from a medical procedure on his injured foot, Mac McClung did not accompany the team to New York. Ömer Yurtseven did not start, but returned to action off the bench.<ref name=boxscore20200311>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=401210943 St. John's vs. Georgetown – Box Score – March 11, 2020 – ESPN Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref> During the first half, the Hoyas shot 54.5 percent from the field<ref name=ap20200311/> and Terrell Allen scored 18 points, reaching 1,000 points for his college career with his 15th point.<ref name=bancroft20200311>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/3/11/21175783/hoyas-end-another-frustrating-season-with-more-questions-than-answers Bancroft, Bobby, "Hoyas End Another Frustrating Season With More Questions Than Answers," casualhoya.com, March 11, 2020, 10:33 pm EDT Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref> In contrast, St. John's struggled to mount a consistent offense during the half<ref name=ap20200311/> and shot only 2–for–13 (15.4 percent) from three-point range.<ref name=ap20200311/> The Hoyas led 42–33 at halftime,<ref name=ap20200311/> and they quickly extended their lead to 15 points in the second half,<ref name=ap20200311/> jumping out to a 48–33 advantage with 18:31 remaining.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/playbyplay?gameId=401210943 St. John's vs. Georgetown – Play-by-Play – March 11, 2020 – ESPN Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref> Georgetown still led 62–52 with 6:31 left to play<ref name=ap20200311/> when the game's momentum shifted entirely to St. John's. During the remainder of the game, Georgetown did not score, missing all 10 shots it took and committing four turnovers.<ref name=ap20200311/> Meanwhile, St. John's finished the game with a 23–0 scoring run,<ref name=ap20200311/> during which Red Storm sophomore forward Marcellus Earlington scored 10 straight points.<ref name=ap20200311/> St. John's enjoyed its biggest comeback of the season by far<ref name=ap20200311/> and its largest in its 41 years of play in the Big East tournament,<ref name=barish20200313>[https://thehoya.com/mens-basketball-georgetown-gives-up-15-point-lead-in-1st-round-loss-to-st-johns/ Barish, Austin, "St. John’s Knocks Georgetown Out of Big East tournament," thehoya.com, March 13, 2020 Retrieved March 21, 2020]</ref> and the Red Storm knocked Georgetown out of the tournament with a 75–62 victory,<ref name=ap20200311/> the Red Storm's third straight defeat of the Hoyas in a Big East tournament game.<ref name=ap20200311/> Terrell Allen scored 21 points<ref name=boxscore20200311/> and Jamorko Pickett finished with a double-double (13 points and 10 rebounds),<ref name=ap20200311/><ref name=boxscore20200311/> while Yurtseven scored eight points and grabbed six rebounds in 21 minutes of play.<ref name=boxscore20200311/> The loss brought Georgetown's season to an end and left the Hoyas winless in the Big East tournament since [[2016 Big East men's basketball tournament|2016]].<ref name=bancroft20200311/> They finished the season with a record of 15–17, their third losing season in five years, first since the [[2016–17 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2016–2017 season]], and first under Ewing, whose Big East tournament record as head coach fell to 0–3.<ref name=bancroft20200311/>

St. John's advanced to play top-seeded Creighton in the first game of the quarterfinals on March 12 and was leading at halftime when the Big East announced the cancellation of the game and of the remainder of the Big East tournament in an effort to reduce large gatherings of people during the growing [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>[https://www.si.com/college/2020/03/12/big-east-tournament-canceled-halftime-game-coronavirus West, Jenna, "Big East Plays One-Half of Quarterfinal Game Before Canceling Tournament at Halftime," si.com, March 12, 2020 Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref><ref name=espntournamentcancelled20200312>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28893285/ncaa-tournaments-canceled-coronavirus Anonymous, "NCAA tournaments canceled over coronavirus," espn.com, March 12, 2020 Retrieved March 16, 2020]</ref> It was the last college basketball game played during the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–2020 NCAA basketball season]];<ref name=espntournamentcancelled20200312/> later that day, the NCAA cancelled all postseason basketball tournaments in 2020, bringing the 2019–2020 season to a sudden end.<ref name=espntournamentcancelled20200312/>

===Wrap-up===

Plagued by roster problems which began with December's scandals and transfers and were compounded in February and March by injuries to its two top scorers, the 2019–2020 Georgetown team had a tumultuous, frustrating, and disappointing season.<ref name=bancroft20200311/> Projected preseason to finish sixth — and perhaps higher — in the Big East, the Hoyas finished in a tie for eighth, and they failed to win a Big East tournament game for the fourth straight season. The NCAA's cancellation of the 2020 NCAA Tournament and 2020 NIT occurred before selections for those tournaments could take place, but Georgetown's sub-.500 finish ensured that it would not have returned to the NCAA Tournament and made even an NIT appearance very unlikely.<ref name=bancroft20200311/> Had the NCAA Tournament taken place, the Hoyas thus would have missed it for a fifth straight year anyway, their longest absence from the tournament since their 31-season NCAA tournament drought from 1944 through [[1973–74 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1974]]. For the fifth straight season, the Hoyas never made the Top 25 in either the [[Associated Press Poll]] or the [[Coaches Poll]] – the first time that had happened in five consecutive seasons since the Hoyas' 23-year absence from the rankings between [[1953–54 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1953]] and [[1976–77 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|1977]].

The team played with great heart in spite of its loss of players<ref name=casual20200313>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/3/13/21176697/links-hoyas-worn-down-by-st-johns-at-seasons-end-allen-mosely-pickett-blair-yurtseven-wahab-mcclung Whipple, "LINKS: Hoyas Worn Down by St. John’s at Season’s End," casualhoya.com, March 13, 2020, 8:00 a.m. EDT Retrieved March 21, 2020]</ref> and had some notable successes during the year, especially the six-game winning streak that followed the departure of Akinjo and LeBlanc and the upset win on the road over No. 19 Butler with both McClung and Yurtseven sidelined by injury. However, the team played so shorthanded from December onward that fatigue took its toll as the season wore on, with the few remaining scholarship players getting little rest during games and having little energy left even for practices;<ref name=casual20200313/> Ewing resorted to having former players — such as recent graduates Kaleb Johnson, Greg Malinowski, and Trey Mourning — join the team for practices to fill out a practice squad, and in March Malinowski told ''[[The Washington Post]]'' that the practices had become less physically demanding than the ones he remembered while playing for Ewing during the 2018–2019 season in order to allow greater rest for the healthy scholarship players, of which only six remained at the end of the regular season.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/03/10/georgetown-basketball-practice-roster-big-east-tournament/ Wallace, Ava, "Injuries and transfers have turned Georgetown basketball practice into an alumni game," washingtonpost.com, March 10, 2020, 5:04 p.m. EDT Retrieved March 21, 2020]</ref> Georgetown's lack of depth meant that it could not trade fouls with its opponents, requiring the Hoyas to play less aggressively than they otherwise might have,<ref name=casual20200313/> and opponents took advantage of Georgetown's slim roster by rotating their players in and out frequently and establishing a rapid pace of play to tire out the Hoyas by the second half of games.<ref name=casual20200313/> Relying on inside scoring, the 2019–2020 squad had not shot well from three-point range, and had shown troubling defensive lapses.<ref name=bancroft20200311/>

News of Josh LeBlanc's transfer to [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] broke on January 1,<ref>[https://defpen.com/georgetown-josh-leblanc-transfers-lsu/ Harris, Dylan, "Georgetown’s Josh LeBlanc Transfers to LSU," defpen.com, January 1, 2020, Retrieved March 18, 2020]</ref> and on January 7 [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] announced James Akinjo's transfer to play for the Wildcats.<ref>[https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2020/1/7/21055406/james-akinjo-transfer-arizona-wildcats-basketball-official-georgetown-eligible-depth-chart Kelapire, Ryan, "Arizona officially announces addition of Georgetown transfer James Akinjo," azdesertswarm.com, January 7, 2020, 11:31 a.m. PST Retrieved March 18, 2020]</ref> When he left the team on December 2, Akinjo had played in 40 games in his Georgetown career of one season plus four weeks, starting 39 of them, and averaged 13.4 points and 2.9 rebounds per game, shooting 35.9 percent from the field and 36.1 percent in three pointers.<ref name=sportsrefakinjo/> Leaving the same day, LeBlanc also played for Georgetown for one season plus four weeks, appearing in 39 games, making 22 starts, scoring 342 points on 62.5 percent shooting from the field and 63.6 percent from three-point range, averaging 8.8 points and 6.6 rebounds per game.<ref name=sportsrefleblanc/> On January 23, the press reported Galen Alexander's transfer to [[Texas Southern Tigers basketball|Texas Southern]]<ref>[https://hbcugameday.com/2020/01/23/georgetown-galen-alexander-transfers-to-texas-southern/ Gaither, Steven J., "Alexander to transfer to SWAC hoops power," hbcugameday.com, January 23, 2020, Retrieved March 18, 2020]</ref> after a seven-week playing career with Georgetown. Myron Gardner quietly transferred to [[South Plains College]],<ref>[https://247sports.com/Player/Myron-Gardner-46055859/ 247sports.com Myron Gardner Retrieved March 18, 2020]</ref> also after only seven weeks of action with the Hoyas.

The season ended with a widespread assumption that Ömer Yurtseven would not return to Georgetown for the [[2020–21 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2020–2021 season]],<ref name=bancroft20200311/><ref>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/3/14/21180179/grammed-omer-yurtseven-announce-the-end-of-his-georgetown-days-patrick-ewing-hoyas-mosely-allen Whipple, "‘GRAMMED: Did Yurtseven Just Announce the End of His Georgetown Days?," casualhoya.com, March 14, 2020, 11:00 p.m. EDT Retrieved March 21, 2020]</ref> and on April 27 he declared for the [[2020 National Basketball Association draft]] and hired an agent, bringing his college eligibility to an end after a single season of play as a Hoya.<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2889009-georgetowns-omer-yurtseven-declares-for-2020-nba-draft-averaged-155-ppg Polacek, Scott, "Georgetown's Omer Yurtseven Declares for 2020 NBA Draft; Averaged 15.5 PPG," bleacherreport.com, April 27, 2020 Retrieved May 27, 2020]</ref> He went undrafted.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/11/24/georgetown-basketball-season-preview/ Copeland, Kareem, "Georgetown basketball searching for a new identity after troubled year," washingtonpost.com, November 24, 2020 Accessed March 10, 2021]</ref> Yursteven had played two seasons at [[North Carolina State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]] before arriving at Georgetown, and over his three-season college career he played in 81 games, starting 61 of them, shooting 53.9 percent from the field and 42.6 percent from three-point range and averaging 12.1 points and 7.1 rebounds per game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/omer-yurtseven-1.html sports-reference.com Omer Yurtseven College Stats Retrieved June 2, 2020]</ref> On May 5, Jamorko Pickett announced he would also enter the 2020 NBA draft, although he retained his college eligibility for the time being.<ref name=casual20200505>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/5/5/21248675/mac-mcclung-back-patrick-ewing-seems-to-think-so-omeryurtseven-jamorko-pickett-nba-draft-andy-katz Whipple, "MAC McCLUNG BACK? Ewing Seems to Think So," casualhoya.com, May 5, 2020 6:00 p.m. EDT Retrieved May 19, 2020]</ref> Ultimately, he returned to Georgetown for the following season.

Confusion over Mac McClung's plans arose during the spring. On March 29, he surprised many observers by announcing his intention to enter the 2020 NBA draft while taking steps to maintain his college eligibility if he withdrew from the draft by June 15.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28968201/georgetown-mac-mcclung-test-draft-waters Givony, Jonathan, "Georgetown's Mac McClung to test draft waters," espn.com, March 29, 2020 Retrieved May 19, 2020]</ref><ref name=casual20200329>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/3/29/21198952/declared-mac-mcclung-to-test-nba-draft-waters-links Whipple, "DECLARED: Mac McClung to Test NBA Draft Waters," casualhoya.com, March 29, 2020, 7:00 p.m. EDT Retrieved May 19, 2020]</ref> After Ewing told the press on May 5 that he understood that McClung would return to Georgetown for the 2020–2021 season, McClung's agent disputed it, saying that McClung remained in the draft,<ref name=casual20200505/> and McClung's representatives later told the press that Ewing's comments may have influenced how NBA teams viewed McClung.<ref name=copeland20200522>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/05/22/patrick-ewing-coronavirus/ Copeland, Kareem, "Georgetown Coach Patrick Ewing tests positive for coronavirus," washingtonpost.com, May 22, 2020 Retrieved 23 May 2020]</ref> Finally, on May 13, McClung announced that he had withdrawn from the NBA draft and would transfer from Georgetown in an effort to gain collegiate experience elsewhere as a point guard, which NBA teams had urged him to do, rather than in the shooting guard role he played with the Hoyas.<ref name=casual2020513>{{cite web |url=https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/5/13/21234022/mac-mcclung-to-transfer-from-georgetown-nba-draft-waters-ewing-recruiting |author=Whipple |title=Mac McClung to Transfer From Georgetown |website=casualhoya.com |date=2020-05-13 |access-date=2020-05-23}}</ref> McClung told ESPN, "It was a number of different events that made me feel I had no choice but to transfer from Georgetown. I really wanted to stay, but things throughout my career made me realize that I couldn’t. I’m looking for a place I can call home, a place I can be a part of a family and help them succeed."<ref name=casual2020513/><ref name=russell20200527>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/05/27/former-georgetown-guard-mac-mcclung-announces-transfer-texas-tech/ Russell, Jake, "Former Georgetown guard Mac McClung announces transfer to Texas Tech," washingtonpost.com, May 27, 2020, 7:05 p.m. EDT Retrieved May 27, 2020]</ref> On May 27, he announced that he would transfer to [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]] for the [[2020–21 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|2020–2021 season]]<ref name=russell20200527/><ref name=cbssportsmcclungtransfer>[https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mac-mcclung-transfer-former-georgetown-guard-chooses-texas-tech-as-destination/ Boone, Kyle, "Mac McClung transfer: Former Georgetown guard chooses Texas Tech as destination," cbssports.com, May 27, 2020 Retrieved May 27, 2020]</ref> and apply for a waiver from the NCAA requirement to sit out a season after transferring.<ref name=cbssportsmcclungtransfer/> McClung finished his two seasons at Georgetown with appearances in 50 games, 49 of them starts, averaging 14.2 points and 2.8 rebounds per game, shooting 39.3 percent overall and 29.5 percent from three-point range.<ref name="sportsrefgu20192020"/> McClung's departure meant that Ewing had lost his entire 2018 class of recruits — Akinjo, Leblanc, Grayson Carter, and McClung — to transfer,<ref name=casual20200329/> and it capped off the Hoyas' tumultuous 2019–2020 season. McClung was the fifth Georgetown player to transfer since December and the eighth in Ewing's three years as head coach.

Georgetown's season began in November with great promise and high expectations. The Georgetown program and its fans had expected a breakout season in which the Hoyas performed well in Big East play, returned to the NCAA Tournament for the first time in five years, and put themselves in a position to build further for the 2020–2021 season.<ref name=barish20200517>[https://thehoya.com/commentary-georgetown-basketball-looks-for-light-at-the-end-of-the-tunnel-in-light-of-mcclung-departure/ Barish, Austin, "Georgetown Basketball Looks for Light at the End of the Tunnel in Light of McClung Departure," ''The Hoya'', May 17, 2020 Retrieved May 19, 2020]</ref> Even before McClung announced his exploration of NBA draft prospects in late March, however, at least some observers felt that by the time it ended on a seven-game losing streak, with a record little better than that of [[John Thompson III]]'s final year as head coach in the [[2016-17 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2016-2017 season]] and with a depleted roster, the 2019–2020 season instead represented a step backward for the program, with no real progress toward a return to the NCAA Tournament and national prominence during Ewing's three years as head coach.<ref name=bancroft20200311/> McClung's transfer heightened these concerns; the hope that in 2020–2021 Georgetown would reestablish itself as an elite team, nationally ranked and likely to resume annual NCAA Tournament appearances, had been replaced by an expectation of another rebuilding year in 2020–2021 in which real success in the Big East and an NCAA Tournament bid were unlikely.<ref name=barish20200517/> The loss of five players to transfer, the graduation of Jagan Mosely, and Yurtseven's departure for a professional career left Georgetown with only two players on its roster who would be seniors the following season and the likelihood of having seven or more new faces on that team.<ref name=bancroft20200311/> Its offseason needs included securing graduate transfers among its recruits to season what otherwise promised to be a young and inexperienced team in 2020–2021.<ref name=bancroft20200311/> With three open scholarship positions left to fill even before the loss of McClung opened up a fourth,<ref name=casual20200319>[https://www.casualhoya.com/2020/3/19/21171878/links-ewing-recruits-grad-transfers-bruner-marfo-mcgowens-nolley-burton-walton-lewis-geeter Whipple, "LINKS: Ewing, Staff Still Active on Recruits and Grad Transfers," casualhoya.com, March 19, 2020, 3:00 p.m. EDT Retrieved March 21, 2020]</ref> and under great pressure to find both top talent and players whose character issues would not lead to a repeat of the scandals of December,<ref name=casual20200319/> Ewing and his staff had begun an aggressive recruiting effort by mid-March, reportedly exerting a greater effort to assess the character and "coachability" of players before recruiting them.<ref name=casual20200319/>

The disappointing 2019–2020 season left Georgetown's fan base split in its feelings about Ewing.<ref name=casual20200313/> Ewing had demonstrated talent as a head coach under difficult circumstances,<ref name=barish20200517/> but the transfers of 2019–2020, as well as three other transfers and two dismissals of players from the program during Ewing's three-year tenure as head coach, made it unclear that he could retain the talent he recruited and raised concerns that there might be systemic problems in the program.<ref name=barish20200517/> The program and its fans hoped that the loss of Mac McClung was the final step in moving on from Ewing's failure to retain any of the recruiting class of 2018. With the COVID-19 pandemic sweeping the world in the spring of 2020 — Ewing himself announced on May 22 that he had tested positive for [[COVID-19]] and was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the Washington, D.C., area;<ref name=copeland20200522/> his son, former Georgetown player and assistant coach [[Patrick Ewing Jr.]], announced on May 25 that he had left the hospital and was recovering at home<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29219979/georgetown-hoyas-men-basketball-coach-patrick-ewing-hospital-coronavirus-diagnosis Anonymous, "Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball coach Patrick Ewing out of hospital after coronavirus diagnosis," espn.com, May 25, 2020 Retrieved May 26, 2020]</ref> — it was unclear whether a college basketball season would be played in 2020–2021, but if the season took place, the hope at Georgetown was that the team could use it to build toward a more successful future,<ref name=barish20200517/> perhaps with a return to the NCAA Tournament during the [[2021-22 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|2021-2022 season]].<ref name=barish20200517/>

==Attendance==
Georgetown averaged 7,939 fans per home game during the 2019–2020 season, 66th among the 351 [[NCAA Division I]] teams and a 10 percent increase over the 30-year low of 7,212 they averaged per game [[2018–19 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|the previous season]].<ref name=hoyasaxaattendance>[http://www.hoyasaxa.com/sports/archives/archive0820.htm#5 hoyasaxa.com Georgetown Attendance Up 10% August 12, 2020 Accessed March 1, 2021]</ref> On average, a Georgetown game filled Capital One Arena to 38.6 percent of its capacity.<ref name=hoyasaxaattendance/> In Big East Conference home games, the Hoyas averaged 8,854 fans per game, which was eighth out of the ten teams in the conference<ref name=hoyasaxaattendance/> and on average filled Capital One Arena to 43.1 percent of its capacity.<ref name=hoyasaxaattendance/>
